name: Whirlpool Rapids Bridge
connectingPointsDisplay: Niagara Falls, Ontario — Niagara Falls, New York
facts: The Whirlpool Rapids Bridge, originally the Lower Steel Arch Bridge, opened in 1897 after replacing the 1855 suspension bridge, becoming the longest arch bridge of its time with a 168‑meter span.
In 2009, a major refurbishment replaced catwalks, steel beams, and rivets, while Amtrak assumed maintenance of the rail deck in 2012, leaving only the Maple Leaf service to cross the bridge.
The bridge’s lower deck, converted to asphalt in 1967, now carries only NEXUS‑eligible vehicles, charging a $6.00 USD toll electronically for cross‑border travel between Canada and the U.S.
